title: Best Grok Bot Plugins for Job Search and Applications in 2026
summary: Can Grok Bot apply to jobs for you? Tsenta reviews 2026’s Grok Bot plugins for job search, résumé tailoring and tracking, and what still needs an agent.
body_markdown:
**The best Grok Bot plugins for job search in 2026 are Himalayas and Employed, two job-search MCP servers you add as custom connectors, and Firecrawl, a plugin in Grok Bot’s app catalog whose job-postings skill finds and checks live openings.** For résumé tailoring and tracking, the useful add-ons are user-shared Bot templates such as Headhunter, Resume Optimizer, Job Application Assistant, The Jobfinder and JobGod, because Grok Bot’s own marketplace lists no Bot for job seekers. None of them submits applications on its own. Headhunter and Job Application Assistant say they apply only with your approval, and the others leave applying to you. If that is the step you want handed off, Tsenta is an MCP server that connects to your AI assistant and submits applications on supported company career sites. Tsenta has no Grok Bot guide yet, so we cover it as the alternative, not as a listed plugin.


Published November 20, 2026. Tsenta publishes this guide and sells an applying agent. We checked Grok Bot’s docs, the x.ai marketplace and every plugin and template page linked here that day, but did not run signed-in applications in Grok Bot. Plugins come first, then templates by type. A template’s listing is its author’s claim, not a test result.


## Bots, templates and plugins: what Grok Bot calls each one


People use “Grok Bot plugin” for three different things, and Grok Bot’s docs keep them apart:


- **Marketplace Bots.** The[Grok Bot marketplace](https://x.ai/bot/marketplace) is a curated list of ready-made Bots in nine categories. On November 20, 2026, none was built for job seekers. Its job-related Bots serve employers and sales teams: Recruiting Coordinator schedules interview loops, Talent Discovery finds candidates and Hiring Signals tracks hiring for prospecting.
- **Bot templates.** Anyone can share a copy of their Bot on an x.ai link.[Grok Bot’s docs](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/bots) say “Shared templates are created by other users, not by Grok Bot,” and each template page says the Bot “was created by a third-party user, not by SpaceXSI,” the company name on x.ai’s pages. A template carries a Bot’s description, skills and routines. Every job-seeker Bot below is a template, except Job Search Crew, a paid service.
- **Plugins.** This is the maker’s word for an app or MCP server you connect under **Connect apps** , and a custom server is saved with **Add plugin** .[The docs](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/how-grok-bot-works) say “Bots can use other services through plugins and custom MCP servers,” and the[overview’s](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/overview) “Browse all apps” link goes to the[Cursor Marketplace](https://cursor.com/marketplace) .[Grok Bot signs in with your Cursor account](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/faq) .


A plugin gives your Bots tools, such as a job search or a tracker. A template gives a Bot instructions and a schedule, and works through Grok Bot’s browser and your connected apps.[The docs](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/computer-and-apps) add that a connected app is available to every Bot you run.


## Can a Grok Bot plugin apply to jobs for you?


No plugin we found does. Himalayas, Employed and Firecrawl’s job-postings skill each say they do not submit applications. Apart from Firecrawl, the job-related plugins in the Cursor Marketplace serve employers, such as applicant tracking systems for recruiters, and none applies for a candidate.


Grok Bot itself can try. Each Bot works on a cloud computer with a browser, signs in with logins saved in Vault and fills in saved contact details.[Its docs](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/computer-and-apps) list the steps it hands back to you: single sign-on or a passkey, a CAPTCHA it couldn’t get past, an approval on another device or a QR code, a bank card verification and a site that explicitly requires a human.[The FAQ](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/faq) adds that some sites block traffic from cloud computers. No Grok Bot docs page mentions job applications or résumés.


A dev.to post from August 31, 2026,[“I Let Grok Bot Apply to Software Engineering Jobs While I Was Sleeping,”](https://dev.to/bobbyhalljr/i-let-grok-bot-apply-to-software-engineering-jobs-while-i-was-sleeping-n62) describes a routine that runs every 4 hours, applies to roles it scores 75 or more out of 100 and caps each run at 10 applications, but reports no submitted count, confirmations or replies. The author’s verdict: “Would I let Grok Bot blindly submit 60 job applications every day? Absolutely not.”


So a Grok Bot routine can attempt applications, with you on hand for the steps it hands back. See[how AI agents apply to jobs](https://tsenta.com/blog/how-ai-agents-apply-to-jobs-2026) for where applying agents stop.

## Grok Bot plugins for job search


### 1. Himalayas: remote job search and a tracker, with its own Grok Bot guide


Himalayas is a remote job board with a hosted MCP server at` https://mcp.himalayas.app/mcp` and a[Grok Bot guide](https://himalayas.app/docs/apply-to-jobs-using-grok-bot) dated August 30, 2026. Its public tools for job search, salary data and company research need no account. Saving jobs and moving them through[its tracker’s](https://himalayas.app/mcp) six stages, from saved to archived, needs a free Himalayas account.


It does not apply. The guide says “Himalayas does not auto-submit applications yet” and suggests asking Grok Bot for the employer’s application link, which a Bot can open in its cloud browser. As of November 20, 2026,[Himalayas’ pricing page](https://himalayas.app/pricing) lists one free AI résumé, cover letter and mock interview on its site, Plus at $9 a month for unlimited use and Max at $29 a month.


The guide calls Himalayas “the native remote job board for Grok Bot,” but Grok Bot’s docs do not mention it. Its setup starts from Settings, then Plugins, while[Grok Bot’s docs](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/computer-and-apps) describe **Connect apps** and **Add a custom connector** , so follow Grok Bot’s menus if they differ.


Where Himalayas wins: free search with no sign-in, and it is the only job plugin here whose maker publishes Grok Bot setup. It covers remote roles on Himalayas only.


### 2. Employed by Guaq AI: roles from employers’ own career sites


[Employed by Guaq AI](https://github.com/Guaq-AI/employed-plugins) is a remote MCP server at` https://jobs.guaqai.me/mcp` that signs in with OAuth in your browser. Its maker says it indexes roles from about 5,000 employers’ own career sites. Its tools cover search, company profiles, a ranked feed, alerts for companies you follow and an application tracker, and it labels visa sponsorship “stated” when the posting says so and “likely” when it infers it from the posting and the employer’s history.


Its README says the plugin “never applies for you or contacts anyone.” Its install guide covers more than 20 assistants but not Grok Bot by name. The independent directory[grokbot.dev lists it as a Grok Bot plugin](https://grokbot.dev/plugins/employed/) , and it is the kind of hosted server Grok Bot’s docs say you can add as a custom connector. On[its site](https://jobs.guaqai.me/) , a free preview shows your first 15 matches, and Pro and Ultimate show every match. It showed us prices in local currency, so check yours.


Where Employed wins: it is not limited to remote roles, and the sponsorship labels help if you need a visa.


### 3. Firecrawl: the app catalog plugin with a job-postings skill


[Firecrawl](https://cursor.com/marketplace/firecrawl) is a web search and scraping plugin in the Cursor Marketplace, the catalog Grok Bot’s docs link to, and it signs in through your browser. Its[job-postings skill](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-cursor-plugin/blob/main/skills/job-postings/SKILL.md) searches for roles that match your title, location and limits, then opens each employer posting to check that it still accepts applications. It returns a shortlist with the title, employer, location, advertised pay, required qualifications, your fit or gaps, any deadline and the direct application link, and labels postings it could not verify.


The skill says it does not apply, contact employers or create alerts, and Firecrawl keeps no job tracker. As of November 20, 2026,[Firecrawl’s pricing page](https://www.firecrawl.dev/pricing) lists a free plan with 1,000 credits a month, about 500 searches, and Hobby at $19 a month billed monthly for 5,000 credits. Grok Bot’s docs say you can ask a Bot to add a catalog app, so ask it to add Firecrawl and sign in when the **Connect** card appears.


Where Firecrawl wins: it works for any role or location, and it checks that each posting is live before listing it.


## Job finder templates


### 4. Headhunter: ranked openings checked on employer sites


[Headhunter by Brian](https://x.ai/bot/JWyArDklTr6y7KB06lqRY) “finds and ranks openings matching your profile, verifies every one live on the employer’s own careers site, and keeps your application tracker up to date.” It “Never applies or reaches out without your approval,” and its listing describes no résumé tailoring.


### 5. Job Hunt Bot: a daily shortlist scored against your résumé


[Job Hunt Bot by matt](https://x.ai/bot/yFcyx8WyOfB38IjqetoHX) searches the major job boards and company career pages every day, scores each job against your résumé and LinkedIn profile and sends you the best fits. It “never applies or sends anything without your OK.”


### 6. Hirely: a shortlist plus help applying with confirmation


[Hirely by Parvaneh](https://x.ai/bot/k2oD619wjcM9RMybbtExW) “shortlists verified roles from employer careers pages, helps you apply with confirm-before-submit, and tracks follow-ups.” It is the closest job finder here to applying, but its listing says it asks you to confirm before each submit, and like every template it works through Grok Bot’s browser, so the hand-back steps above apply.


## Résumé optimizer templates


### 7. Resume Optimizer: tailor one résumé to one posting


[Resume Optimizer: Tailor Resume to Job by GrokBotGod](https://x.ai/bot/rEba1S2MuOrKRmLRbEflv) takes your résumé and one job post and returns it “reworded in that post’s words plus a list of gaps to answer, as text, Word or PDF.” It “Never adds jobs, skills, dates or numbers,” and its listing describes no job search or applying.


Where it wins: that no-invention rule is stricter than tools that rewrite freely, including Tsenta’s Aggressive mode, which our own docs say may stretch claims. Our guide to[assistant connectors that tailor résumés](https://tsenta.com/blog/ai-assistant-connectors-tailor-resume-2026) compares the options.


### 8. Job Application Assistant: résumé, cover note and fit note per posting


[Job Application Assistant by Ray](https://x.ai/bot/3cymtsAFCEoIB3gpHAv4a) finds openings, keeps your master résumé polished and “tailors an ATS-friendly resume, cover note, and fit note to each posting as PDFs.” It “never applies anywhere without your explicit yes for that specific role.”


## Tracker templates


### 9. The Jobfinder: a Notion tracker fed by recruiting email


[The Jobfinder by Daniel](https://x.ai/bot/eSCwViGduTgMD6PiOo7jm) , spelled “the j*bfinder” on x.ai, “Keeps a Notion application tracker current from recruiting email, and nudges about upcoming deadlines.” It was built for a career and internship search.[grokbotlist.com](https://grokbotlist.com/bots/the-jobfinder/) lists Gmail as its required app and says it nudges you “rather than replying for you.” Expect to connect Notion and Gmail.


### 10. JobGod: one coach with a Google Sheets tracker


[JobGod by Devin](https://x.ai/bot/-ZNR2GLCmvAdhZ4r_6XA2) bundles a setup wizard, a Google Sheets tracker, “gated scout digests,” résumé tailoring on approval and “apply packets.” Its listing ends with “you always click Apply.”


## A paid service that runs as a Bot


### 11. Job Search Crew: one Bot that watches your target companies


[Job Search Crew](https://jobsearchcrew.com/) is a subscription, not an x.ai template. It sets up “One bot in Grok Bot” (or in[Meta’s Muse](https://tsenta.com/blog/meta-muse-apply-to-jobs-2026) ) that checks your target companies several times a day, rates each new opening from 1 to 10, alerts you at 7 and above and drafts the application, with records in your own Google Sheets and Drive. You review and apply. As of November 20, 2026, it lists the first month free, then $19.99 a month, and needs a Google account.


## Hiring-activity monitors


### 12. Hiring Signals and Competitor Watch: built for sales, usable for target companies


Neither marketplace Bot was built for job seekers.[Hiring Signals by Simon Lackowski](https://x.ai/bot/marketplace/bots/hiring-activity-monitor) “Tracks hiring activity across selected companies and job sources” for prospecting, and its setup asks for a sales role.[Competitor Watch by Shimecki](https://x.ai/bot/marketplace/bots/competitor-watching) “Tracks competitor pricing, product, and hiring pages” from a list of URLs you paste. You could paste the careers pages of companies you want to join, but expect briefs written for competitor research.


## Templates that say they apply for you


Some user-shared templates say they submit applications. These are claims from their x.ai listings, and none of their pages shows results:


- [Remote Job Hunter by TKR](https://x.ai/bot/Jx7uzFMG-dQ9q636btZrS) : “Finds remote openings on company career sites, applies on the employer’s ATS.”
- [Career by Agatho](https://x.ai/bot/_N179jA-vyUT8mlNn2xOs) : “submits through official employer ATS, and keeps an evidence-backed apply log.”
- [Apply Bot by Kyle](https://x.ai/bot/2GdkYgGlc91A6d6MPXCkZ) : “applies at volume.”
- [Application Team Lead by Bennett](https://x.ai/bot/ufmS2cx8QpmyouPNIAkZC) : “farms applications out to helper bots for fast parallel submits.”
- [Job Hunter by Douglas](https://x.ai/bot/nnuIT_YnNzddYfkAxOm0D) : “Applies to jobs for you every day on Indeed, ZipRecruiter, and LinkedIn.”


Each runs through the same Grok Bot browser, so the hand-back steps still apply. If you try one, set an **Ask first** rule in Auto Review, which[Grok Bot’s docs](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/approvals-security-and-privacy) say always produces an approval card. Run it on two or three roles and check each employer’s confirmation email, not the Bot’s log.


## The alternative when you want applications sent: Tsenta


Tsenta is an MCP server that connects your AI assistant to your Tsenta account. Your assistant can get roles ranked against your profile from the 300,000+ company career pages Tsenta watches and start applications that Tsenta submits in the cloud on supported company career sites. Tsenta tailors your résumé for each role in Honest or Aggressive mode, or sends it as written, and drafts a cover letter when the form takes one. Your assistant can also check application status, manage your tracker and read recruiter emails in your Tsenta inbox.


With résumé auto-approval off, each tailored résumé waits for your approval, and form review stops before the final submit on employer systems that support pausing. Auto Apply, which submits eligible roles without per-role approval, needs Power. On Starter and Pro, you choose each role and Tsenta submits it. Your first 25 applications are free, once, with no card. Global USD monthly plans are Starter at $19 for 600 applications, Pro at $39 for 1,500 and Power at $99 for 4,500 per 30-day cycle. See[pricing](https://tsenta.com/pricing) for local prices.


Where the Grok Bot options win: Himalayas and Firecrawl are free to start, Resume Optimizer refuses to add facts, and Grok Bot’s browser can attempt sites Tsenta does not support. Tsenta is not in Grok Bot’s marketplace or app catalog.


### Can you add Tsenta as a Grok Bot plugin?


Possibly, because[Grok Bot’s docs](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/computer-and-apps) say you can add a remote MCP server yourself, and Tsenta’s server is hosted with OAuth sign-in. Tsenta does not publish a Grok Bot guide yet, and we have not tested this route end to end. Following Grok Bot’s docs:


1. Complete your Tsenta profile in the dashboard, including your address and location, which an assistant cannot set.
2. In the Grok Bot desktop app, open **Connect apps** and choose **Add a custom connector** .
3. Enter a **Name** , such as Tsenta, pick **Remote HTTPS** and paste` https://api.autojobs.me/api/v1/mcp` .
4. Choose **Add plugin** , then sign in to Tsenta and approve if Grok Bot asks you to **Authenticate** . You can also ask a Bot to add the MCP server by its address.
5. Start with a read-only ask, such as “Show me three matching roles and explain why each fits,” and check which Tsenta tools Grok Bot lists.


One approval gives the assistant every available Tsenta tool on your account, including tools that edit your profile, move tracker entries and reply to emails. Whether it asks before each action depends on the assistant, not on Tsenta, and in Grok Bot a connected app is available to every Bot you run, including imported templates. Add an **Ask first** rule for applying. On a team, your admin’s MCP policy can block the server from being saved.


### Documented routes: Claude connector and ChatGPT app


For a setup Tsenta documents, add the same server as a[Claude connector](https://tsenta.com/connectors/claude) ;[Claude’s help center](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-get-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp) lists custom connectors on every plan, with one on Free. In ChatGPT it is a ChatGPT app, which OpenAI now calls a plugin, and applying needs full MCP support, which[OpenAI’s help center](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12584461-connecting-custom-mcp-servers-in-chatgpt) lists on Business, Enterprise and Edu on the web. Cursor and Codex work too.[Tsenta’s setup page](https://tsenta.com/mcp) and the[help article](https://help.tsenta.com/connect-claude-chatgpt-mcp) have the steps, and[this walkthrough](https://tsenta.com/blog/connect-ai-job-search-agent-to-claude-chatgpt-2026) covers one end to end.


Comparing assistants? See the best[Claude connectors](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-claude-connectors-job-search-2026) ,[ChatGPT apps](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-chatgpt-apps-job-search-2026) and[OpenClaw skills](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-openclaw-skills-job-search-2026) for job search, what[Instinct connectors](https://tsenta.com/blog/instinct-ai-connectors-job-search-2026) can do, and how[Meta Muse, Grok Bot and Instinct compare](https://tsenta.com/blog/meta-muse-vs-grok-bot-vs-instinct-job-search) .


## What Grok Bot costs for a job search


As of November 20, 2026,[The X Subscription’s pricing](https://docs.x.ai/x-subscription/pricing) includes Grok Bot on Premium at $30 a month or $300 a year, Super at $100 a month and Ultra at $200 a month. The $8-a-month Plus plan does not include it. Usage draws on a weekly pool shared across Grok, Grok Bot and Cursor, with top-up credits beyond it.[Grok Bot’s FAQ](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/faq) says some accounts get a trial: a usage credit with a 7-day window. A routine that browses career sites every few hours draws more from the weekly pool than a once-a-week shortlist does, so check your usage first.


## A practical Grok Bot job-search setup


1. **Search.** Connect Himalayas for remote roles or Employed for a wider set, or add Firecrawl, and ask for a shortlist with each employer’s application link.
2. **Tailor.** Run Resume Optimizer on the two or three roles you care most about, and answer its gap list yourself.
3. **Track.** Use The Jobfinder, JobGod or the Himalayas or Employed tracker. Our guide to[tracking applications with AI assistants](https://tsenta.com/blog/track-job-applications-ai-assistants-2026) covers more.
4. **Apply.** Open each link yourself, or let a Bot fill the form with an **Ask first** rule on and take over when it hands you a sign-in or CAPTCHA. For an agent that submits, use Tsenta from a documented assistant.
5. **Check.** Count an application as sent only when the employer confirms it.


Our[MCP server comparison](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-mcp-servers-job-search-2026) covers more job servers you can add the same way.


## Frequently asked questions


### What are the best Grok Bot plugins for job search?


The best Grok Bot plugins for job search are Himalayas and Employed, two job-search MCP servers you add as custom connectors, and Firecrawl, a plugin in Grok Bot’s app catalog whose job-postings skill finds and checks live openings. For résumé tailoring and tracking, user-shared Bot templates such as Resume Optimizer, Job Application Assistant, The Jobfinder and JobGod fill the gaps. None of them submits applications without your approval for each role.


### Is there a Grok Bot plugin that applies to jobs for me?


No Grok Bot plugin we found applies to jobs for you. Himalayas, Employed and Firecrawl’s job-postings skill each say they do not submit applications, and Grok Bot’s docs never mention job applications. A few user-shared templates say they apply, but none shows results. Tsenta’s MCP server submits applications on supported company career sites, and it possibly works as a Grok Bot plugin you add yourself, because Grok Bot’s documentation says it can add a remote MCP server by its address. Tsenta documents setup for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Codex and has no Grok Bot guide yet.


### Can I use a Grok Bot plugin to apply to jobs automatically?


Not reliably. Grok Bot has a browser on a cloud computer and can fill web forms, so a Bot can try an application. Its docs say it hands you single sign-on, passkeys, CAPTCHAs it cannot pass and sites that require a human, and that some sites block cloud computers. Grok Bot’s maker documents no job applications, so treat any routine that applies for you as an experiment and check each result.


### Does the Grok Bot marketplace on x.ai have a job search or résumé plugin?


No. On November 20, 2026, the curated marketplace at x.ai/bot/marketplace listed no Bot for job seekers, and its job-related Bots served recruiters and sales teams. Job search and résumé Bots exist as user-shared templates on x.ai links, which independent directories such as grokbot.dev and grokbotlist.com collect. Grok Bot’s app catalog lists Firecrawl, whose job-postings skill finds and checks live openings.


### Is there a Grok Bot job application tracker?


Yes. The Jobfinder template keeps a Notion tracker current from recruiting email, JobGod keeps a Google Sheets tracker, and the Himalayas and Employed plugins each include a tracker once you sign in. Grok, the chat app, is a different app from Grok Bot, and these templates run in Grok Bot.


### Can I connect Tsenta to Grok Bot?


Possibly, because Grok Bot’s documentation says it can add a remote MCP server by its address, but Tsenta does not publish a Grok Bot guide yet and is not listed in Grok Bot’s marketplace or app catalog. In the Grok Bot desktop app, open Connect apps, choose Add a custom connector, enter a name, pick Remote HTTPS, paste[https://api.autojobs.me/api/v1/mcp](https://api.autojobs.me/api/v1/mcp) and choose Add plugin, or ask Grok Bot to add the MCP server by its address. Sign in to Tsenta if asked.


### How much does Grok Bot cost for a job search?


As of November 20, 2026, Grok Bot comes with The X Subscription’s Premium plan at $30 a month, Super at $100 and Ultra at $200, and the $8 Plus plan does not include it. Usage draws on a weekly pool shared with Grok and Cursor. The job-search templates show no price, and Himalayas, Employed and Firecrawl have their own free tiers and paid plans.


### Are Grok Bot templates on grokbot.dev or grokbotlist.com official?


No. Both are independent directories that say they are not affiliated with xAI, and they link to templates hosted on x.ai. Grok Bot’s docs say shared templates are created by other users, not by Grok Bot, and each template page says the Bot may act on your behalf. Read what a template does and which apps it expects before you add it.
